newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian court upholds sacked MP's jail term.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian court upholds sacked MP's jail term.

text.p: Sacked Indonesian legislator Sri Bintang Pamungkas said on Thursday the High Court had upheld a lower court decision to sentence him to 34 months in jail for defaming President Suharto.
"I received the verdict on December 30, saying the (Jakarta) High Court has upheld the jail sentence. I will appeal against the decision to the Supreme Court," Bintang told Reuters.

The Central Jakarta District Court sentenced Bintang last May to 34 months in jail for defaming Suharto during a speech he made to Indonesian students in Berlin in April 1995. Bintang was out on bail while appealing the decision.
Bintang, a 50-year-old university lecturer, said he would maintain he was innocent. He added that he had not received an order from the court to send him to jail.
Bintang said in October he would stand for president in 1998 polls to highlight the need for political change.
He was sacked by the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) in 1995 for being too outspoken. The decision was subsequently approved by Suharto.

After his conviction in May, Bintang, along with lawyer and former student activist Julius Usman, set up the United Democratic Party of Indonesia (PUD), defying a law that recognises only three political parties in the country.
The PPP, the ruling Golkar party and the Christian- Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only parties legally permitted to contest general elections due in May this year.
Suharto has been re-elected unchallenged for six consecutive terms since 1968 and is likely to run for a seventh term.
